query: What travel policy risks appear in expense descriptions?

per_column.name: asset_category
per_column.rationale: A taxonomy of asset/expense types (hardware, cloud, travel_item). This is a general classification of the expense, not an aspect of travel policy risk itself. At best it is context that could predict risk, not a part-of the risk concept.

per_column.name: transport_expense_misclassified
per_column.rationale: Misclassification of a transport expense is a genuine constitutive aspect of travel policy risk -- a specific type of policy-compliance problem embedded in the description.

per_column.name: asset_description_quality
per_column.rationale: Descriptive quality (specific_model, vague_generic) is a property of the text that may signal risk, but it characterizes description quality, not a part of travel policy risk per se.

per_column.name: entry_method
per_column.rationale: How the entry was created (manual vs automated) is a process/provenance attribute that may cause errors, but it is not a facet OF the risk itself.

per_column.name: missing_source_id_flag
per_column.rationale: Absence of a source ID is a data-completeness flag on the record, a possible indicator of risk, not a constitutive aspect of travel policy risk.

per_column.name: processing_lag_flag
per_column.rationale: Processing delay is a workflow-timing attribute; it may correlate with risk but is not a part-of the policy-risk concept.

per_column.name: repeat_user_flag
per_column.rationale: Whether a user appears repeatedly is a behavioral/frequency attribute external to the risk concept, not an aspect of the risk itself.

judge.rationale: Only one column (transport_expense_misclassified) is a genuine constitutive facet of travel_policy_risk -- an actual policy-compliance violation type. The remaining columns are external predictors, causes, or irrelevant taxonomies: asset_category is a generic expense classification; asset_description_quality, missing_source_id_flag, processing_lag_flag and repeat_user_flag are metadata/data-quality signals that may correlate with risk but are not aspects OF it; entry_method is a provenance cause. The set therefore does not carve the concept into non-overlapping constitutive aspects (many overlap as 'data-quality/process anomaly' proxies), and coverage of the actual sub-dimensions of travel policy risk (e.g., unauthorized spend categories, out-of-policy amounts, missing approvals, duplicate/personal expenses, timing/limit breaches) is almost entirely absent.
